newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Italy urged to submit fresh EMU convergence plan.
newsitem.headline: Italy urged to submit fresh EMU convergence plan.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azelio Ciampi told the European Commission on Monday it would soon submit a fresh convergence plan for economic and monetary union (EMU), a Commission spokesman said.
The spokesman, briefing reporters on a meeting between Ciampi and European Economic Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy, said Italy had not presented a complete programme since 1992.

He said Ciampi and de Silguy had not discussed specific efforts that Italy was making to qualify for the single currency, but that de Silguy had pressed Ciampi for an updated economic convergence plan.
The Commission has also asked Belgium, Germany, Ireland, Portugal and France to submit revised plans. Belgium and Germany have already done so, the spokesman said.

The Commission needs such plans in particular to assess whether EU countries are running excessive budget deficits. It found in 1996, when it last carried out the exercise, that the programmes of the six countries mentioned were "outdated".

Ciampi, who was in Brussels to meet various European commissioners, plans to hold a news conference later in the afternoon on the Commission's concerns about Italy's failure to use EU regional development funds. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
